h1:
Mookata & BBQ in Suphan Buri
8 Cheap Dinner Spots
intro: Suphan Buri has so many mookata (Thai BBQ hotpot) places it's genuinely hard to pick one. Come evening, locals just default to meeting up at a grill spot — anywhere from a few-hundred-baht all-you-can-eat mookata to Korean BBQ and a riverside seafood buffet. We rounded up 8 places that have real reviews and decent value, all easy dinner picks when you're in town.
chips: 💸 Filling for a few hundred baht

blocks.html: Ask anyone in Suphan Buri what to eat for dinner and the answer you'll hear most is mookata. Grill spots are spread across the town center, U Thong, and Song Phi Nong, and most are buffets in the low hundreds where you can sit and graze all night. Some have seafood to grill, some have live music. We've split them into groups by the kind of vibe you're after, with rough prices and the area each one is in. The prices here are ballpark and can shift with whatever promo is running, so it's worth checking the restaurant's page before you go.

blocks.text: Mookata buffets — the real deal in Suphan Buri

blocks.html: This is mookata the way Suphan Buri locals actually eat it: a buffet in the low hundreds with pork, seafood, fried bits, veg, and a punchy dipping sauce. Most open from evening into the late hours, ideal for a group of friends or family.

items.name: Ton Khun Mookata-Seafood Buffet (opposite Wat Phra That)
items.blurb: One of the mookata spots Suphan Buri locals bring up most often. The buffet covers both pork and seafood like shrimp and crab, grilled or boiled, all you can eat, plus fried items and desserts. The thing a lot of people love is the bold dipping sauce. Prices start in the low hundreds and include drinking water.
items.meta: Opens evening, around 4pm · opposite Wat Phra That, Mueang district

items.name: Pae Mookata Branch 3 (Clock Tower junction)
items.blurb: A long-running place locals know by name. The draw is the long hours — open from late morning to midnight — with mookata sets in the low hundreds, grilled prawns, grilled fish, plenty of fried options, and live music on Thursday-to-Sunday evenings. Easygoing spot to settle in for a while.
items.meta: Open 10am–midnight · Clock Tower junction, heading toward Route 340

items.name: Mam Mam Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: An in-town mookata buffet that reviews pretty well. Good variety for a price in the low hundreds, works for a big group, and parking is easy. A no-overthinking dinner pick.
items.meta: Opens evening · Mueang Suphan Buri district

items.name: Kratha Thong Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: Another buffet locals recommend, leaning into all-you-can-eat value. You get pork, seafood, and fresh veg — good for anyone who likes to take their time grilling. Friendly on the wallet.
items.meta: Opens evening · Mueang Suphan Buri district

items.name: Jan Jao Mookata, U Thong branch
items.blurb: The mookata option over on the U Thong side, handy if you're staying or sightseeing around the U Thong ancient town and don't want to drive into the city. Buffet in the low hundreds, with solid fresh ingredients and a decent dipping sauce.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: A lot of Suphan Buri mookata places only open in the evening and get packed on Friday and Saturday. If you're rolling in with a big group, try calling ahead or messaging the restaurant's page so you're not stuck waiting for a table.

blocks.text: Half a day with a local who knows the lanes — or cooking a dish yourself — teaches you more than just eating. Book ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide.

blocks.html: If you want a change of pace from the round-pan mookata, Suphan Buri has Korean- and Japanese-style grill spots with nicer interiors — good for photos and a cool, air-conditioned room.

items.name: Umai Yakiniku Buffet Suphan Buri
items.blurb: A Japanese-style grill buffet decked out with pink cherry-blossom trees for a faux-Japan feel. Air-conditioned, lots of tables, Wi-Fi available. It's split into classic and premium courses — the higher one comes with more seafood and beef. Good for anyone who wants to sit, chill, and take photos.

items.name: TON Buffet Korean BBQ (U Thong)
items.blurb: A Korean-style grill buffet on the U Thong side, with fresh seafood that changes daily — the standouts are butterflied prawns and oysters. Time-limited to around 100 minutes. Good for fans of Korean-marinated meats and grilled seafood.

blocks.text: Grilled seafood buffets for the seafood crowd

blocks.html: For anyone who needs seafood with their grill night, this group leans on a fresh seafood bar you load up and grill yourself. Good for a big meal or a special occasion.

items.name: Jom Yut Grilled Seafood Buffet
items.blurb: A grilled seafood and mookata buffet whose selling point is the fresh seafood bar in the middle of the room — several kinds of shellfish, surf clams, hard clams, crab, and fish fillet. Prices are reasonable and there's no time limit. Some seating is by the water, so it's great if you like to take it slow and eat for a while.
items.meta: No time limit · riverside seating area

blocks.title: Get your money's worth on a seafood grill
blocks.html: A grilled seafood buffet pays off most when you go for the higher-cost-per-head items like oysters, prawns, and surf clams — but take it a few pieces at a time. Pile up too much and you can't grill it fast enough, and it just goes to waste.

blocks.text: How to pick the right spot for your dinner

items: Big group on a tight budget — go for an in-town mookata buffet like Ton Khun, Mam Mam, or Kratha Thong: full for a few hundred baht and you can sit a long while.
Want the vibe, somewhere to chill and take photos — Umai, the air-conditioned Japanese grill with cherry-blossom decor, or a place with riverside seating like Jom Yut.
Seafood lover after lots of fresh catch — Jom Yut's seafood buffet, or TON Buffet Korean BBQ in U Thong.
Staying or sightseeing on the U Thong side — Jan Jao and TON Buffet are close by, so no driving into the city center.
Want a late night with live music — Pae Mookata Branch 3 stays open till midnight and has live music on weekends.

blocks.html: All in, a mookata or grill dinner in Suphan Buri runs roughly a couple hundred baht a head, up to four-hundred-plus for a premium course loaded with seafood — good value for how much you can put away. If you're visiting Suphan Buri and want an easy, filling, good-value dinner, grilling is one of the first things locals reach for.

faq.q: Which Suphan Buri mookata is the best value?
faq.a: For all-you-can-eat value in the low hundreds, Ton Khun opposite Wat Phra That comes up a lot because you get both pork and seafood to grill, unlimited, starting around 199 baht including water. If you're after pure seafood, Jom Yut's grilled seafood buffet starts around 279 baht with no time limit.

faq.q: What time do Suphan Buri grill spots open?
faq.a: Most open in the evening from around 4pm onward. A few, like Pae Mookata, run from late morning to midnight. It's worth checking the restaurant's page before you go, since some close on weekdays or change prices with promos.

faq.q: Are there any air-conditioned grill spots in Suphan Buri?
faq.a: Yes — Umai Yakiniku Buffet is an air-conditioned Japanese-style grill with cherry-blossom decor and Wi-Fi, good for anyone who'd rather not sit out in the heat and likes a photogenic setting.

faq.q: Are there mookata places on the U Thong side?
faq.a: Several — for example Jan Jao Mookata's U Thong branch and TON Buffet Korean BBQ, which has fresh seafood. Handy for anyone staying or sightseeing around the U Thong ancient town who doesn't want to drive into the city center.

faq.q: How much is a mookata meal in Suphan Buri per person?
faq.a: A typical mookata buffet runs a couple hundred baht a head, around 199–279 baht. Premium courses or grills with lots of seafood can climb to around 389–399 baht per person.
